task_name: The plugin's groom, driven by this backend

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and I located each one. (a) 'asks ct-groom.mjs what it would create': CtGroomEpic.planned() calls #groom(asked, true), whose argv is [ctGroom, spec, '--repo', repository.text, '--milestone', milestone, '--dry-run'] with { cwd: asked.root.text }, and parses stdout into GroomPlan/GroomPlanIssue keeping milestone and, per issue, order, title and labels. I checked that shape at the source: plugin/scripts/groom.js#groomPlan returns { milestone, issues:[{order, title, body, labels, deps, ac, descripcion, protectedLine, senal, specLink, gates, gatesContent, e2eContent, epicContext..., frozenDecisions...}] } and ct-groom.mjs:1250 prints it with repo and project added, on a stdout the script keeps 'pure, parseable JSON' (its two dry-run notices go to stderr). (b) 'asks it to create it': run() calls the same builder with dryRun false and awaits. (c) 'turning any other exit into a typed failure carrying the program's own words': #groom returns for NO_DIVERGENCE (0) and UNRECONCILED_DIVERGENCE (3) and otherwise throws EpicNotGroomed(said.stderr.trim()); start-plan-route.ts:305 projects it with detail: cause.message, so the plugin's stderr reaches the answer unrewritten. ToolRunner already substitutes failure.message for an empty stderr on a failing exit, so the 'own words' are never empty.

The TDD line names it('the dry run asks for the plan and the real run is never mistaken for it') and fixes the limit as 'argvFor ends in --dry-run for planned and never carries it for run, and the parsed plan holds the milestone and one GroomPlanIssue per issue'. The body at ct-groom-epic.test.ts:117-139 asserts exactly that: dryRunArgv.at(-1) === '--dry-run', realArgv not containing it, and — the half the previous verdict found unpinned — node.calls now equal to [{ argv: dryRunArgv, options: { cwd: Mother.ROOT.text } }] after planned(), so flipping the production line to #groom(asked, false) turns this test red instead of leaving it green. plan.milestone is the milestone and plan.issues are the two GroomPlanIssue of the scripted stdout. Its boundary pair it('exit 3 is the plan all the same and exit 2 is the plugin own words') is there too: exit 3 returns the plan, exit 2 yields an EpicNotGroomed whose message is the scripted stderr with the trailing newline trimmed, which is what the brief itself prescribes (said.stderr.trim()). Same assertion, same input, same expected value as the written phrase.

Name by name against the three Contract blocks. groom-plan.ts: GroomPlanIssue with readonly order/title/labels and constructor({ order, title, labels }), GroomPlan with readonly milestone/issues and constructor({ milestone, issues }) — identical, both frozen at construction with a copied, frozen labels/issues array. ct-groom-epic.ts: 'export class CtGroomEpic extends EpicGroom', static readonly COMMAND = 'ct-groom.mjs', NO_DIVERGENCE = 0, UNRECONCILED_DIVERGENCE = 3, constructor({ node: ToolRunner['run'], ctGroom: string }), static argvFor({ ctGroom, spec, repository, milestone, dryRun }): string[] — identical, and the argv order is the one plugin/commands/ct-groom.md line 6 documents ('<spec> --repo <o/r> --milestone <Epic> --dry-run'). epic-groom.ts: type Grooming = { root, spec, repository, milestone }, async planned(asked): Promise<GroomPlan>, async run(asked): Promise<void>, with the 'must implement' idiom of the named exemplar domain/ports/epic-specs.ts. The errors: EpicNotGroomed for the call that failed and GroomPlanNotUnderstood for the answer we cannot read, both under EpicGroomFailure extends PlanFailure, both joining PlanCollapse with kebab-case codes ('epic-not-groomed', 'groom-plan-not-understood') as the task's sentence 'Both leaves join PlanCollapse here' asks. One remark, not a deviation: Grooming is declared twice (port and adapter) because the brief's block does not export it, and TypeScript's bivariant method parameters would not catch the two drifting.

Rows the diff bears on: D-10 (everything new under backend/ is TypeScript) — all five production files and both test files are .ts and use only erasable syntax; D-11 (the yardstick is imported from the plugin, never reimplemented) — the adapter invokes ct-groom.mjs as a program and forms no second opinion about the spec or the table, it reads the exit code and parses the JSON the plugin printed; D-13 (no phase is stored) — nothing is persisted, the plan is derived on each call from the program's output; D-25 (the plugin composes the context and the backend relays paths) — the adapter hands over the spec's path, the repo and the milestone and pastes no text anywhere. Rows with no subject here: D-1, D-6, D-7, D-14, D-18, D-21, D-22, D-23 — this task adds no endpoint, no gate key, no front, no merge and no promotion. No row is reopened; in particular nothing in the diff writes to a pull request or merges.

Exemplars: the adapter is the shape of backend/src/infrastructure/dispatch-check-workbench.ts — node: ToolRunner['run'] injected, a static argv builder, the cap living in ToolRunner and never chosen here — and the JSON reading follows the gh-* adapters' idiom (JSON.parse in a try, a typed *NotUnderstood quoting what the tool printed). The port matches domain/ports/epic-specs.ts; the value objects are frozen like freeze-finding.ts. Test file: NodeDouble is the exemplar's own double, verbatim in shape; the test names are the spaced sentences the recent spec-freeze tests use. backend/conventions/this-repository.md holds on its own terms: the family names its two causes, the codes are kebab-case, the refusal is 400 via PlanCollapse, and the four-step way of talking to a tool is respected. conventions/defects.md, rule by rule. (1) Closed vocabulary: the two success exits are named constants, there is no string classifier and no boolean standing in for a state; the 'anything else' branch is over exit codes, which are an open set from a subprocess, and folding them into one failure is what the objective and the slice's end state prescribe — not a catch-all over a closed vocabulary. (2) Raw map as the return value of logic: none. planned() returns a frozen GroomPlan of frozen GroomPlanIssue, the parsed JSON never leaves #planIn/#issueIn, and Grooming is a compile-time-checked parameters object, not a return. (3) Two fields that have to agree: none — GroomPlan carries the milestone and its issues with no flag repeating their non-emptiness, and there is no sentinel (an empty stderr cannot reach the message: ToolRunner substitutes failure.message on a failing exit). (4) Errors named for what happens: EpicNotGroomed and GroomPlanNotUnderstood are the two causes conventions/domain.md asks a family to separate; neither is named for a module. Boundaries: the layers and the imports are clean (domain imports domain; infrastructure imports domain), the cap arrives with the injected runner, only the consumed keys are projected — which conventions/boundaries.md explicitly allows for a foreign format with an open vocabulary — every projected field is checked at runtime before use, and the answer's code is declared explicitly beside its detail. Delivery: no document of either yardstick prescribes a shape of change here; the diff adds new symbols and two rows to an existing projection table and breaks no call site. What I weighed and did not turn into findings: the `parsed as { milestone?: unknown, issues?: unknown } | null` at ct-groom-epic.ts:70 and 85 is a cast at a boundary, but every property stays `unknown` and is validated by typeof/Array.isArray immediately after, so no wrong value passes for good — the repo's other doors use a type-guard predicate instead, and that is a preference here, not a defect; and the Mother's provenance line travels inside the payload the double prints, whereas the repo's precedent (backend/__tests__/fixtures/declared-gh-pull-request-reviews.json, read as DECLARED.reviews) keeps `captured` beside the payload rather than in it. The three things the previous verdict ordered are all in this diff, and I re-measured them: planned()'s real invocation is now asserted; the scripted stderr is now the plugin's own English line, verbatim from plugin/scripts/ct-groom.mjs:229; and the declared shape now names its capture — I verified it against the source it names, since the fixture's issues #1 and #2 reproduce rows 1 and 2 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-11-...-execution.md § Tabla de slices field by field (titles, descripcion, protectedLine, senal, ac, gates) and carry the full key set of groom.js#groomPlan, so the projection is measured against a real capture and not a fiction. No mutation-sweep declaration was in the package, so that part of testing.md was not readable to me; it is not a finding against the diff.

The only '-' line in a test file is the FAMILIES row of plan-refusal.test.ts:57, rewritten to add 'EpicGroomFailure' beside the members already there. Nothing is removed or relaxed: FAMILIES is the list of abstract family roots that every_way_the_plan_can_collapse_has_a_refusal_declared excludes from its census, the new root is abstract and is not projected, and the task's **Tests:** line asks for exactly this change ('In plan-refusal.test.ts, FAMILIES gains EpicGroomFailure'). That same exhaustiveness test is what forced the two concrete leaves into PlanCollapse, and both are there, so the assertion ends up stricter rather than weaker.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code: ct-groom-epic.ts builds the argv, applies the cwd, decides on the exit code, raises EpicNotGroomed with the program's own stderr and parses the plan into the frozen value objects of groom-plan.ts, and start-plan-route.ts turns both failures into answers. The test's own scaffolding is only NodeDouble — a recording stand-in for ToolRunner.run, which is the cut right before the external system that conventions/testing.md prescribes for an adapter — and the Mother's inputs. No expected value stands in for a production line: every assertion reads back either what the adapter handed the runner or what it returned, so reverting the production files fails all four tests.

Inside the seven declared files the diff writes only what the task's sentences ask for: the two value objects and the port of the Contract blocks, the adapter with its argv builder, its exit-code branch and its parse, the EpicGroomFailure family with its two leaves, the two PlanCollapse rows and the FAMILIES member. No refactor, rename or adjacent fix rides along, and no import or symbol is added beyond those. Nothing named in ### Out of scope is touched: plugin/scripts/ct-groom.mjs, groom.js, slices.js and gh-issue-map.js are unmodified and the first is only invoked as a program; there is no --reconcile, no --project, no endpoint, no front, no dispatcher change and no repository column. The public statics that could look spare (COMMAND, NO_DIVERGENCE, UNRECONCILED_DIVERGENCE, argvFor) are prescribed verbatim by the Contract block and used by the adapter's own diagnostics and by the TDD test. The diff carries no hunk of the plan file, so there is no amendment to rule on.

Four new tests, all in ct-groom-epic.test.ts. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no network, no filesystem, no randomness, no sleep — the only collaborator is an in-memory double resolving a ProcessOutput built in the test. Isolated: each case builds its own NodeDouble with its own calls array, the Mother's statics are frozen value objects and arrays nothing mutates (GroomPlanIssue copies and freezes the labels it is handed), and no test depends on the order of the file. Verifies real behaviour: the assertions are on the argv the adapter actually handed the runner, the cwd it applied, the GroomPlan it returned and the exception classes and messages it raised — not on a double's call count for its own sake nor on a constant the test just defined. The two failure causes are told apart, each asserted against its own sibling class. I loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development for the finer half: its 'Good Tests' table says "One thing. 'and' in name? Split it", and both prescribed names carry an 'and' — but those two names are written literally in the task's **TDD:** line, so this is the plan clashing with the text the implementer was handed, and I declare it here instead of reporting it. Nothing else beyond the three properties.
